title: Optional argument for --promote-install-files breaks CLI compatibility

approach_note: dra27 (MEMBER, the reporter) proposed a `--promote-install-files` / `--no-promote-install-files` flag pair. bobot (CONTRIBUTOR) agreed at first, then decided not to hold 2.9.1 for it. No maintainer has endorsed a fix since.
open_questions: Is it still worth changing after 5 years? Making the argument mandatory, or switching to a flag pair, would break 2.9+ users who pass `--promote-install-files=false`, so it would need a deprecation cycle. The broader question of a future-proof CLI (#4859) was closed without a decision.
next_step: Maintainers decide whether to close as won't-fix, since the workarounds are known. Otherwise, add `--no-promote-install-files` and deprecate the optional-argument form.
notes: This is a regression from 2.9.0 (2021) that has been in place for about 5 years. opam has already worked around it by putting the flag last, and `--` also works. The reporter later said the problem only occurs if dune makes this kind of change once. The related PR #4859 (unambiguous CLI) was closed in 2023.

title: dune 3.0 cannot find file through relative path during ppx preprocessing

approach_note: rgrinberg (MEMBER) first said the change was intended for cache relocatability (paths not tied to source location) and that using workspace-root-relative paths is the correct workaround. Later he agreed this breaks compositionality and suggested resolving [%blob] paths relative to the preprocessed file, which is mostly a ppx_blob-side change.
open_questions: Should dune give preprocessors a way to recover the source file's directory (cwd, a location mapping, or an env var) without hurting cache relocatability, or should ppxs resolve paths themselves? Also, should the 3.0 change be documented as a breaking change?

active_prs.note: Reproduction test case only; closed without merging

next_step: Document in the preprocessing docs that, from lang 3.0, preprocessors run from the workspace root (sandboxed) and that source paths are workspace-relative, and point ppx authors to a relocation-safe way to resolve files. Then decide whether to close this as a ppx_blob issue.

title: A cram test that writes to one of its own files mutates the shared cache entry for that content
desc: A cram test that runs `chmod +w` and writes to a dependency writes through the symlink sandbox into the hardlinked shared-cache entry, corrupting it for all later restores.
approach_note: rgrinberg: bwrap/landlock help on Linux, but on macOS the only option is defensive copying. Alizter suggested clonefile; no decision yet.
open_questions: Which mitigation to use: copy sandboxing for cram dependencies when the cache is in hardlink mode, clonefile on macOS, or detecting the corruption on restore?
next_step: Add the issue's reproduction as a cram test in the dune test suite (shared cache with a fresh cache root).
notes: Corruption is silent and crosses projects that share the cache root, and it persists until the cache is cleared. Workarounds: `--sandbox copy`, `DUNE_CACHE_STORAGE_MODE=copy`.

title: installing dune with DUNE_BUILD_DIR set fails.
desc: A relative DUNE_BUILD_DIR nested more than one level deep (e.g. .temp/dune) is rejected with a message that says sub-directories of the root are allowed.
open_questions: Should nested relative build dirs be supported, or should the error message just say only direct children are allowed?

notes: Draft PR #16411 (Sudha247) was closed. Implementation is tracked in #16186 and the CLI design in #16430.

title: dune subst fails with opam pin -k path when no version can be determined
desc: With dune lang >= 3.17, `dune subst` errors with 'repository does not contain any version information' when no VCS info is available (as with `opam pin -k path`), but the docs say it does nothing in that case.
approach_note: Alizter (COLLABORATOR) found the error is guarded behind lang 3.17 and that `-k path` does not copy .git. No fix has been endorsed.
open_questions: With no VCS info, should `dune subst` do nothing (as documented), substitute a placeholder version, or keep erroring and have the docs corrected?
next_step: Add a cram test that runs `dune subst` with no VCS and lang >= 3.17, then decide between restoring the documented no-op and updating the docs.
notes: Behavior change behind lang 3.17. Workaround: use lang < 3.17 or `opam pin` without `-k path`. Blocks Deducteam/lambdapi#1482.

title: `_build/default` in `compile_commands.json`'s "`directory"` value
desc: Generated compile_commands.json uses a relative "directory" like `_build/default/bin`, which clangd can't resolve, so it fails to find includes.
approach_note: Alizter (COLLABORATOR) asks why rewriting is needed at all, since ccls copes with the file; no fix endorsed yet.
open_questions: Emit absolute directory paths, or rewrite the paths relative to the project root when promoting? The JSON compilation database format normally expects an absolute "directory".
next_step: Add a cram test showing the directory/file fields, then emit an absolute "directory" in the generated file
notes: The reporter's workaround is a jq post-processing step. Only C stubs users with clangd are affected.

notes: Alizter suggested a workaround: a rule using with-accepted-exit-codes.

title: Allow specifying per-mode linker flags
not_bug_reason: Feature request: per-mode linker flags. A maintainer pointed out that `ocamlopt_flags` already covers the motivating case.
desc: Asks for `ocamlc_link_flags`/`ocamlopt_link_flags` fields so flags like `-linscan` can apply to native links only.
notes: nojb says `(env (dev (ocamlopt_flags -linscan)))` already covers this because `-linscan` is a compile-time flag. The issue could probably be closed.

title: odoc: can't link between packages
not_bug_reason: Feature request: dune's odoc rules don't support cross-package references yet (part of odoc 3 support tracked in #14763). The generated odoc-config.sexp isn't used, and users can't control its contents.
desc: Asks for odoc doc builds (`@doc` and `@doc-new`) to resolve references to another package in the project declared with `(depends (pkg :with-doc))`.
notes: Workaround: `dune build @install && dune exec -- odoc_driver foo foo_unix`. Two gaps remain. The user can't add extra entries (e.g. unix) to the generated odoc-config.sexp, and installing their own copy conflicts with dune's rule. Related: ocaml/odoc#1491 and #1461. shonfeder says work on this is planned.

title: `generate_opam_files` broken in 3.24
desc: Since 3.24, `dune build <pkg>.opam` no longer regenerates the opam file from dune-project. It exits 0 and gives no hint that only `dune build @opam` plus promotion now works.
approach_note: Alizter (COLLABORATOR) says `dune build @opam` is the preferred way now. No fix has been endorsed for the explicit-target case.
open_questions: Should building the `.opam` target directly offer a promotion for that file, or at least warn or fail and point the user to `@opam`?
next_step: Add a cram test showing that `dune build foo.opam` silently does nothing, then make it either promote the file or print a hint pointing to `@opam`.
notes: Regression in 3.24, caused by the behavior change in #14108. punchagan confirmed it still reproduces on main. #16234 is not related.

title: Dune installed via `opam` crashes on `dune init` with SIGSEGV on macOS
not_bug_reason: Not a dune bug: the segfault comes from OCaml being built against the macOS 27 SDK while running on macOS 26 (ocaml/ocaml#15067). The reporter confirmed the CFLAGS workaround fixes it.
desc: opam-installed dune segfaults on `dune init` on macOS 26 because the switch was built with the macOS 27 SDK.
next_step: Close as duplicate of #16413 / upstream ocaml/ocaml#15067
notes: Upstream fix is ocaml/ocaml#15071. Workaround: set CFLAGS to the MacOSX26 SDK sysroot and run `opam switch reinstall`.

title: rfc(cram): allow runner to abort test
not_bug_reason: RFC/feature proposal: a way for a cram test to abort so its failing output isn't cached.
desc: Proposes letting cram tests abort (via an exit code or a `cram_abort` helper) so the rule fails and its output is not cached.
notes: rgrinberg (MEMBER) prefers a hidden `cram_abort` shell function over user-chosen exit codes. Alizter also wonders whether `--force` support for cram tests would be simpler.

title: Register sandbox cleanups with the scheduler
desc: Sandbox cleanups are fiber finalizers that the scheduler skips on shutdown, so sandbox directories can be left behind.
approach_note: Alizter (COLLABORATOR): register sandbox cleanups directly with the scheduler so they always run on shutdown.
next_step: Add a scheduler-level cleanup registry and move sandbox cleanup onto it, with a test that interrupts a build and checks the sandbox is removed
notes: Assigned to chizy7 (2026-09-30). Came out of PR #16415. Related to #16478 (always produce a unique sandbox directory).

title: Go testscript as a cross-platform CRAM alternative?
not_bug_reason: RFC/feature request: a cross-platform, shell-free alternative to cram tests (Go testscript).
desc: Proposes supporting Go's testscript format as a cram alternative that works on Windows without a POSIX shell.
approach_note: rgrinberg prefers pluggable third-party cram engines (like inline test runners) over building testscript support into dune.

title: Strange dependency cycle error on build with no cycles
desc: With (lang dune 3.23), a (copy_files ../file.txt) causes a spurious dependency cycle because the compile_commands.json rules eagerly compute directory contents.
approach_note: Alizter (collaborator) traced the cycle to the compile_commands.json rules and is drafting a fix in #16518; the reporter suggested evaluating Dir_contents lazily, only for stanzas with foreign stubs.
open_questions: Whether a lazy Dir_contents lookup is enough, or whether the cycle can still happen when foreign stubs are actually used.
